chunks: Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
If you appear with an opponent before a governor or before a judge, then stand at his right.

key_terms.خَصْمٍ: an opponent or litigant in a dispute
key_terms.يَمِينِهِ: his right side; the instructed position to stand

ai.seo_question: What is the proper etiquette when appearing before a judge with an opponent in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches an etiquette to be observed when appearing with an adversary before a ruler or judge. It reflects orderly conduct and proper decorum in judicial or governing settings.
